thread:
Alex: heads-up — PeregrineHealth is seeing p99 tail spikes on their dedicated pool since ~03:00 UTC. They hit our SLA threshold and opened an escalation. Logs look like repeated routing retries.
Maria: thanks for flagging. do we have a quick mitigation? can we route them to a lower-capacity fallback model to reduce latency while we investigate?
Sam: looking at the routing logs now — I see a surge of 502s from pool-13 proxy -> model-host. same request ids repeating. suspect kv-cache eviction + retry loop on long-context requests.
Jen: @Sam can you paste the errors? need to loop oncall and customer success with an ETA.
Sam: paste of recent lines:
```
2024-07-14T03:04:21Z pool-13 proxy ERROR request_id=aa12 retry=3 upstream=10.4.2.11:5043 connection_reset
2024-07-14T03:04:21Z model-host WARN kv_cache_miss seq=8192 model=gpt-medium
2024-07-14T03:04:22Z proxy INFO routing fallback_count=2 selected_variant=quant8-small
```
Dmitri: kv cache churn + retries makes sense. quick mitigation: disable aggressive prefetch on pool-13 and lower batch window to 4ms. That should reduce p99 while we fix the root cause.
Claire: customer-facing update needed — we should promise "short-term mitigation applied, investigating root cause, ETA for fix: 6h". is 6h realistic?
Sam: I can cut a canary hotfix to reduce batch window and disable prefetch. PR drafted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/8273 — needs review.
Alex: assign owners: Sam = hotfix + canary rollout, Dmitri = cache investigation/root cause, Jen = coord w/ CS and PeregrineHealth, Maria = monitoring & postmortem. Agree?
Maria: agreed. I'll spike temporary alert suppressions for noisy retries and add a dashboard panel for Peregrine p50/p95/p99.
Jen: looping in ops-bot to create incident and page rotation.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-0895, severity=P1, channel=#incident-INC-2024-0895. Pages: oncall-team -> Sam, Dmitri.
Sam: canary plan: deploy to pool-13 small canary (5% traffic) at T+15m, monitor 5min windows x3 -> if stable roll to 30% then full. Rollback command: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/serving-proxy -n pool-13`.
Dmitri: for RCA I'm attaching a quick repro command to simulate long-context eviction locally:
```
python tools/evict_repro.py --seq-len 8192 --concurrency 12 --pool pool-13
```
Claire: CS note: sending PeregrineHealth this message: "We've applied a short-term mitigation and are performing a careful rollout. We'll confirm a stable window or next steps within 60 minutes and share a 6-hour tech ETA for a full fix." ok?
Alex: that's fine. final ask: Sam, can you post the PR link + canary roll timestamps and update this thread when each step completes? Jen pls post the customer messages. Dmitri keep RCA progress notes here.
Sam: PR merged to staging -> canary deploy started at 03:18 UTC. pinging when 5% stable.
Dmitri: seen reduced kv-cache churn on canary logs so far. still validating seq=8192 runs.
Jen: emailed CS update to PeregrineHealth and pasted in the thread. they acknowledged and asked for an SLA credit timeline if issue persists.
Alex: capture SLA credit discussion separately with finance; primary is stability now. thanks all — update thread with any regressions. :thumbsup:
Maria: monitoring shows p99 dropped from 1.8s -> 700ms on canary. moving to 30% in 10m.
ops-bot: Update: INC-2024-0895 status=investigating -> mitigated (short-term). Next steps: RCA, long-term fix, postmortem due in 48h.
Sam: 30% -> 100% rollout complete at 03:42 UTC, no rollback needed. marking hotfix as deployed.
Dmitri: RCA note (initial): root cause = premature kv-cache eviction on models with long-seq patterns + retry loop in proxy. Fix planned: adjust eviction policy + add backpressure on retry logic. assigning follow-up PRs.
Claire: logged customer follow-up and postmortem expectation to CS. will schedule 1:1 if Peregrine wants deeper review.
Alex: great work. I'll create a short checklist for postmortem owners and timeline. closing slack escalations once the postmortem draft is shared.
